T-ORDER.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases: discount then points then rounded tax, cap/no excess consumption, fully-discounted zero floor and FR multi-line rounding pass.

T-LOTS.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: expired/empty lots skipped, earliest-expiry-first partial and four-lot allocations match exact ledger balances; other customer untouched.

T-IDEM.evidence: 6/6 frozen cases: original-result replay, changed-body rejection, foreign replay denial, tax-change stability and concurrent identical/mismatched keys all pass under a customer-level boundary.

T-RACE.evidence: 0/4 frozen cases stop at the unchanged GET quote missing points; supplemental 2/6/12/20-request yielding fixtures conserve all reported debits.

T-REVERSAL.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases: original lot IDs/expiry restored, mixed-expiry and all-expired shares forfeited, repeated cancellation does not restore twice; debit/cancel share a compatible boundary.

T-AUTH.evidence: 3/3 frozen cases: missing session 401, foreign spend and foreign cancellation 403/404 with unchanged ledgers; replay is authorized and supplemental changed-owner replay rejects 404.

T-PENDING.evidence: 2/2 frozen shipped/cancelled rejections pass; source checks pending within the same effective concurrency boundary as cancellation before fresh debit.

T-CLOCK.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: injected now is used, expiry is exclusive at equality, and advancing to expiry selects the later lot.

T-FAIL.evidence: 3/3 frozen pricing failures leave lots unchanged because quote is computed before writes, but supplemental second saveLot rejection leaves the first 81-point allocation debited.

T-EFF.evidence: 1/3: fresh/next records 10 -> 3010 (budget 36), six calls; replay one call/two records; lotsFor has no usable-history filter/index.

1. Order, conversion and rounding.why: T-ORDER 4/4: quoteWithPoints caps requested/spendable cents after discount, then computes rounded tax and nonnegative total.

2. Lots and clock.why: T-LOTS 2/2 and T-CLOCK 2/2: usableLots uses injected time with strict expiry, sorts earliest-first and spendPoints records partial allocations.

3. Idempotency including mismatch.why: T-IDEM 6/6: route authorizes inside withCustomerLedger before stored quote/fingerprint lookup; lookup, debit and saveRedemption are in the same effective customer boundary.

4. Customer concurrency and failure atom.why: ledger-lock.ts covers full spend/refund workflow with finally release and supplemental races conserve points, but a second saveLot fault leaves an uncompensated first-lot debit before receipt publication.

5. Reversal and expiry.why: T-REVERSAL 4/4: allocation lot IDs and status applied/reversed restore only live original lots and prevent repeat reversal under the same lock.

6. Authentication and ownership.why: T-AUTH 3/3 and supplemental ownership-change replay 404: owned-order checks precede all redemption, cancellation and replay use cases.

7. Pending-only eligibility.why: T-PENDING 2/2: pending check and writes are under withCustomerLedger shared by cancellation, so a fresh redemption cannot race a stale state.

8. Efficiency.why: Fresh/next full-history lotsFor reads cost 10 -> 3010 records (budget 36), six calls; writes are allocation-proportional and replay one call/two records but there is no usable-lot index.

9. Layering and pure domain.why: Pure pricing/allocation/returnPoints rules and application services exist, but routes still own locking/cancellation orchestration rather than thin application delegation.

10. Final-report honesty.why: Public rerun confirms 22/22 and 13 added tests; report explicitly discloses unchanged GET quote, partial-write non-atomicity, in-process locking and absent static checking.
